os-learning-s01-006.category: Section 01 — Linux, the terminal and your first commands
os-learning-s01-006.title: Use and reuse command history
os-learning-s01-006.instructions:
Practise navigating and reusing your shell history.

Run the following commands in exactly this order:

1. pwd
2. whoami
3. date
4. echo HISTORY_REPEAT_PREVIOUS
5. !!

The !! shortcut should repeat your previous command. You should therefore see HISTORY_REPEAT_PREVIOUS printed twice.

Continue with:

6. echo HISTORY_BY_NUMBER
7. history

Look at the numbered history output and find the number belonging to the command echo HISTORY_BY_NUMBER.

8. Use !n to execute that command again. Replace n with its actual history number. For example, when the command is numbered 12, enter !12.

Finally:

9. Run history > history-practice.txt to redirect your command history into a file.
10. Run cat history-practice.txt to inspect the saved history.

Your file must contain evidence of the commands being executed in the correct order.
hints: !! repeats the immediately preceding command.
history displays your commands with their corresponding numbers.
!n executes a command using its history number. Replace n with the actual number shown by history.
The history number changes depending on how many commands you have executed.
The > operator redirects output into a file, overwriting its previous contents.
Use cat history-practice.txt to inspect the saved history.
Do not clear your history during this exercise.

Require the referenced command and its specified arguments: echo HISTORY_BY_NUMBER
Require the referenced command and its specified arguments: history
